correctness.rationale: From the exact binary EF1 predicate, each participant violates precisely when its own pair is 00 and at least one rival pair is 11. Agent row independence gives the product formula. The geometric-mean critical function is strictly increasing, proving unique global minimization and monotonicity. A logarithmic analysis at that root proves the all-n asymptotic including loglog and constant; exact enumeration independently matches 18 rational examples, and numeric root checks supplement rather than substitute for proof.

evidence: Chen–Long Section 4.2 gives an algorithm-uniform worst-input EF1 success upper bound with deterministic valuation inputs, not a Bernoulli-utility chance for any fixed partition.
Bu et al. establishes existence of lotteries with support-wide ex-post fairness when valuation vectors are known; it cannot be substituted for a specific frozen allocation under unknown realization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither stronger-sounding guarantee covers the measured stochastic experiment. The fixed-assignment chance can be arbitrarily small while an allocation chosen after valuations are observed can satisfy EF1.
searches: "best of both worlds" binary valuation EF1 ex ante ex post

evidence: Chen–Long upper-bounds the confidence achievable by randomized algorithms against worst deterministic inputs; the present conclusion fixes all goods assigned in pairs and varies an unknown Bernoulli parameter.
Bu et al. conditions on known binary utility profiles to design allocation lotteries; the candidate does not optimize over those lotteries.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The previous results do not imply or subsume the claimed formula, unique minimizing parameter, strict population monotonicity, or second-order rare-rate logarithmic expansion. A claim of general EF1 impossibility does not establish an exact success probability under the markedly narrower probabilistic experiment.

evidence: Chen–Long arxiv:2609.23577v1 defines probability over online algorithm randomization with deterministic values (Section 2.1); its EF1 impossibility relies on a finite distribution of adversarial instances (Theorem 4.3).
Bu et al. arxiv:2410.06877v1 Section 2 defines randomized assignments over fixed valuation profiles, distinct from stochastic utility realization.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: EF1 as a predicate is shared, but fixed predetermined balanced bundles with i.i.d. random valuations is not equivalent to randomizing allocation conditional on a fixed valuation instance. No distributional equivalence or parameter identification turns the earlier EF1 guarantee into this p-dependent success law.

evidence: The inspected primary sources give proofs and general guarantee bounds, not an exact table or formula for the n-dependent optimizing Bernoulli parameter.
The new verifier enumerates n=2..6 cases as a proof cross-check; it is not a pre-existing published table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No located database or table evaluated this exact probability, its single-root condition or asymptotic profile. A failed search is not a uniqueness proof, and unknown indexed or unindexed earlier work remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: Two goods per participant are the minimal natural regime in which nonnegative additive EF1 can fail. The exact all-n rare-parameter minimizer, strict population drift and second-order log-scale failure law identify structural instability of a canonical ex ante fair assignment before binary values are known; this is more informative than finite numerical examples and is not entailed by correctness alone.
